fidelity.interpretation: Local fidelity compares the fitted surrogate's evaluation at the explained instance with an actual model call at the same instance. Weighted R^2/RMSE summarize surrogate fit over the kernel-weighted perturbation sample; the holdout value is computed on a seeded disjoint split. A small instance error alone is NOT evidence of neighborhood fidelity - see the quality assessment for the verdict.

explanation.interpretation_note: LIME weights are weighted local-linear surrogate coefficients for 'field keeps the explained instance's value' versus 'field takes a reference value from the decoded training background'. Under the default fixed_background_reference scheme that reference is a single fixed decoded-background vector (numeric median, categorical mode) reused by every perturbation row; under the optional sampled_background_marginals scheme each field instead draws its reference from the background marginals per perturbation row. Neither scheme samples a real patient record. LIME weights are NOT Shapley values, do NOT decompose the prediction exactly, are NOT additive in probability units, and may differ from exact SHAP attributions in magnitude and sign. They describe model sensitivity in a local perturbation neighborhood—never causality, never clinical risk, and never clinical advice.
limitations: LIME is a local weighted-linear approximation of the declared model output; it is not an exact Shapley decomposition and carries no efficiency/local-accuracy guarantee.

Surrogate weights are conditional on the perturbation sampling scheme, kernel width, ridge penalty and random seed; the reported fidelity and seed-stability diagnostics quantify but never eliminate this sensitivity.

Neither preserves inter-feature correlations of the development cohort, and no perturbation row is a reconstructed real patient record (a documented distributional approximation).

criteria.name: effective_samples
criteria.rationale: Weighted regression precision collapses when the kernel-weighted effective sample size is small.

criteria.name: design_condition_number
criteria.rationale: Ill-conditioned weighted normal equations destroy coefficient precision regardless of the fitted values.

criteria.name: surrogate_weights_finite_and_nonzero
criteria.rationale: Non-finite or all-zero coefficient vectors carry no local information (1.0 = every weight finite with a non-zero maximum).

criteria.name: instance_target_value_finite
criteria.rationale: Both the actual model output and the surrogate value at the instance must be finite to report any fidelity measure.

criteria.name: attribution_count_matches_feature_count
criteria.rationale: Every registered panel field must receive exactly one attribution or the feature lineage is incomplete.

criteria.name: local_fidelity_relative_error
criteria.rationale: Absolute instance-level guard for targets close to zero; the primary instance criterion is the sigma-scaled error below.

criteria.name: local_fidelity_error_in_neighborhood_sigma
criteria.rationale: Scale-free instance error: the surrogate must reproduce the model's own output at the explained point to within a fraction of the neighborhood's output spread.

criteria.name: weighted_r2
criteria.rationale: Share of the kernel-weighted model-output variance the surrogate explains across the sampled neighborhood.

criteria.name: holdout_weighted_r2
criteria.rationale: Variance explained on a seeded disjoint split of the same neighborhood; prevents in-sample-only acceptance.

criteria.name: stability_assessed
criteria.rationale: A verdict without repeated perturbation draws cannot distinguish a reproducible weight from sampling noise.

criteria.name: stability_min_pairwise_spearman
criteria.rationale: Rank agreement of the full weight vector across seeds.

criteria.name: stability_sign_agreement_fraction
criteria.rationale: Fraction of seed-pairs whose coefficient signs agree; near-zero weights may legitimately flip sign, hence < 1.

criteria.name: stability_top_k_overlap_fraction
criteria.rationale: Agreement of the highest-|weight| fields across seeds, the part of the explanation a reader actually ranks.
